issues.issue: "Best efforts" is undefined and the clause supplies no benchmark, cost ceiling or required action against which either party's protective efforts could be measured. It is also mutual and open-ended, so what protection either owes is indeterminate.

The flat bar on Licensee filing "any document requesting any governmental authority to take any action" affecting the Marks cannot be squared with clause 2(b)(iii), which expressly authorizes Licensee to prepare and file registration documents as Licensor's agent when Licensor defaults. The two provisions give opposite instructions on the same filings.

The prohibition on using, selling or displaying "any merchandise bearing such designations" cannot be squared with clause 2(b)(vii), which expressly permits merchandise bearing the Exhibit D designations to be sold for eighteen months, nor with 2(b)(iv)'s merchandise regime. Whether merchandise may bear "Hard Rock" location or area designations is answered differently by the two clauses.

"Licensor will always have full control of any joint proceedings" with costs and recoveries shared equally sits against the preceding sentence giving each party an independent right to sue at its own cost and keep its own recovery, and the clause never says when a proceeding becomes "joint". Nor does it say who decides to make an action joint.

The indemnity covers "any suits, loss and damage arising out of any service or act rendered or performed by Licensee ... in relation to the Hard Rock Hotel Marks, or the Hard Rock Casino Marks", language broad enough to reach claims caused by Licensor's own conduct or by defects in the licensed marks. There is no carve-out, cap, notice or control-of-defense mechanism to bound it.

The cross-promotion duty applies only "when practical and appropriate", a standard with no benchmark and no decision-maker named. Whether a party ever breaches by omitting the other's facilities cannot be determined from the clause.

The table-tent display Licensor must place in its own restaurants referencing Licensee's facilities must be "reasonably acceptable to Licensor", which appears to be a mechanical error for Licensee and leaves the obligor as the sole judge of its own performance. As written the sentence gives Licensor an approval right over material it alone supplies.

"Any book written or sponsored by Licensor or its affiliates which describes the Hard Rock Facilities and/or history" leaves "sponsored", "history" and the required prominence of the Morton credit undefined. Whether a brochure, website or coffee-table book triggers the duty is not fixed by the words.

The equal-treatment duty applies only to a map "which identifies all locations where there is a Hard Rock Facility", so a map identifying fewer than all locations escapes the clause entirely. "Same size and style" is also unmeasured.

An agreement "to discuss the possibility" of mutual sponsorship fixes no obligation, standard or outcome and is an unenforceable agreement to agree. Nothing in it identifies what a breach would look like.

Licensor's right to develop web pages for "other Hard Rock Facilities as they may develop" cannot be squared with the exclusive license to the Hotel and Casino Marks in the Morton Territories granted by Section 2(a), since Hard Rock Facilities include Licensee's Hotel/Casinos. The Licensee-only carve-out for the Territories and the Internet sales rules in 2(b)(v) leave the boundary of each party's web rights contested.

A license "granted in perpetuity" with no termination provision cannot be squared with Section 16, which presupposes "the termination of this Agreement", or with 3(b)'s reference to "the Term of this Agreement". Whether any breach can end the license is left unanswered by the instrument read as a whole.

"Licensee shall be solely entitled to all economic benefits" of the licensed rights cannot be squared with Section 6(d), which divides recoveries from infringement actions in the Morton Territories equally, or with 3(c)'s vesting of all goodwill in Licensor. The clause claims exclusivity over benefits the contract elsewhere splits.

The first-offer right rests on a duty to "initiate negotiations and to negotiate in good faith" with no price, terms or objective standard, an agreement to agree whose breach is unmeasurable. "All or substantially all of his assets and/or rights" also fixes no threshold for what triggers it.

The unrestricted right to "sublicense or franchise any or all of the rights and licenses granted hereunder" cannot easily be squared with the first-offer right in Section 9(c), since a sublicense of all rights would transfer the business without triggering negotiation with Licensor. Nothing in either clause says which governs a wholesale sublicense.

The clause stipulates irreparable harm generally for Licensor but for Licensee only as to the single Nevada prohibition in clause 3(a), so expressio unius suggests money damages are the measure for every other Licensor breach. The asymmetry is on the face of the provision and would be argued both ways.

The no-waiver-by-delay rule sits against Section 22, which permits waiver of any term by a signed written notice of the benefited party alone, without stating how the two interact. Whether conduct short of a signed notice can ever waive a right is left to be worked out between the clauses.

The notice address "In the case of Licensor" is Hard Rock Cafe International (DEL), Inc., a different entity from Rank Licensing, Inc., which the preamble and Section 1(n) define as Licensor. Which entity is entitled to receive and give notices, and whether the discrepancy signals an assignment, is not resolved.

The declaration that "under no circumstances shall any power be granted or deemed to be granted to Licensee or be deemed to be coupled with an interest" cannot be squared with clause 2(b)(iii), which appoints Licensee to file registrations "for Licensor as Licensor's agent and in Licensor's name". The section's carve-out addresses agency only and not the coupled-with-an-interest sentence.

The requirement that all claims be prosecuted in New York courts "except as provided in Section 5" cannot be applied without deciding which disputes Section 5 sends to arbitration, and Section 5(a) fixes an arbitration forum alternating between California and New York. The forum for a mixed quality-control and infringement dispute is therefore contested between Sections 5 and 14.

The survival clause presupposes "the termination of this Agreement", but Section 9(a) grants the license in perpetuity and the contract contains no termination right or procedure. Reading the two together, it is unclear whether the parties contemplated any termination at all.

The integration clause makes the entire understanding consist of this Agreement "together with the Purchase and Sale Agreement", a document neither defined, dated nor attached anywhere in the instrument. What terms are thereby included, and how a conflict between the two would be resolved, cannot be answered from the text.

Binding the agreement upon and to the benefit of "transferees and assigns" without qualification sits against Section 9(c), which conditions a transfer of substantially all rights on a first-offer negotiation, and Section 10's sublicense terms. Whether a transferee takes free of those conditions is not answered by either provision.

The unqualified representation of power and authority sits against Section 2(a)'s ownership warranty, which is expressly cut back "subject only to whatever actions or inactions may have been taken or not taken by Morton". Whether the Section 19 representation carries the same qualification is unresolved between the two.

"The valid and binding agreements of all of the Parties hereto" uses a capitalized term, "Parties", that the contract never defines, and speaks of plural "agreements" where there is one. The parenthetical carve-out for "general equitable principles" is likewise unbounded.

The representation is given by and about "the Morton Parties" and "the Rank Parties", terms that appear nowhere else in this Agreement and are nowhere defined. Who makes the noncontravention representation, and about whose commitments, cannot be determined from the instrument.

Permitting unilateral waiver of "any of the terms or conditions" by written notice of the benefited party alone cannot be squared with Section 17 and Section 23, which allow modification only by a written instrument executed by each party. A one-sided waiver of an obligation and a bilateral amendment of it are the same act described two ways.

Providing that the Agreement may be "interpreted at any time only by written instrument duly executed by each of the parties" is an odd use of "interpreted" that on its face would purport to bar construction by anyone but the parties jointly. What effect that word has, if any, is a question on the face of the clause.

Exhibit C's asterisk notes permit the geographic designation to be "replaced with 'Beach Club' or 'Athletic Club' as designations" without the limits clause 2(b)(vi) imposes — use only within the confines of the facility and not for merchandise. The exhibit, which 2(b)(vi) makes the controlling model for logo use, and the clause cannot both be given full effect.
